# Fix: UV workspace Python environment not available in per-node flake pipelines

## The Problem

When a T pipeline uses both **UV workspace Python resolver** (`[py-dependencies] resolver = "uv"`) and **per-node custom flakes** (e.g. `node(..., flake = "github:jbedo/rshells")`), Python nodes fail with:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pandas'
```

...even though `flake.nix` correctly builds the UV workspace environment with pandas.

**Root cause:** The `pipeline.nix` template (generated by `populate_pipeline`) has two places
where the Python environment is constructed:

1. **`projectPyEnv`** — the project-level Python environment, used by nodes without a custom
   flake. **Correctly handles UV** by using `pySet.mkVirtualEnv` from `uv2nix`/`pyproject-nix`
   when `pyResolver == "uv"`.

2. **`mkNodeEnv`'s `py-env`** — the per-node Python environment, used when a node has a custom
   `flake = ...`. **Always uses** `pkgs.${pyVersion}.withPackages`, the old nixpkgs resolver.
   When `resolver = "uv"`, `pyPackagesList` is `[]` (packages come from `uv.lock`, not
   `tproject.toml`), so the resulting environment has no packages at all.

```nix
# pipeline.nix, inside mkNodeEnv — line 139 — NOT UV-aware:
py-env = pkgs.${pyVersion}.withPackages (ps: [ ps.deepdiff ] ++ (builtins.map (p: ps.${p}) pyPackagesList));
```

Result: Python nodes with custom per-node flakes get a bare Python with no pandas, while
project-default Python nodes work fine because they use `projectPyEnv`.

## Relevant Files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `src/pipeline/nix_emit_pipeline.ml` | Generates the `pipeline.nix` template (lines 111–234) |
| `src/pipeline/nix_emitter.ml` | Thin wrapper re-exporting `nix_emit_pipeline` |

The template is a `Printf.sprintf` format string that emits Nix code. All the relevant lines
are literal Nix embedded in the OCaml template — no runtime logic, just text substitution.

## The Fix

**File:** `src/pipeline/nix_emit_pipeline.ml`, line 139

**Before:**
```nix
      py-env = pkgs.${pyVersion}.withPackages (ps: [ ps.deepdiff ] ++ (builtins.map (p: ps.${p}) pyPackagesList));
```

**After:**
```nix
      py-env = if pyResolver == "uv" then projectPyEnv
               else pkgs.${pyVersion}.withPackages (ps: [ ps.deepdiff ] ++ (builtins.map (p: ps.${p}) pyPackagesList));
```

**Why this works:** `mkNodeEnv` is defined in the same `let ... in` block as `projectPyEnv`,
so `projectPyEnv` is already in scope. When `pyResolver == "uv"`, the per-node flake's Python
environment just reuses the project-level UV workspace environment. This is correct because UV
dependencies are managed independently of which nixpkgs revision the per-node flake pins — they
come from `uv.lock`.

**Trade-off:** When UV is active, the per-node flake's nixpkgs version is ignored for Python
dependencies. This is acceptable — UV manages Python dependencies independently of nixpkgs.

## How to Test

The `py_uv_per_flake_t` demo in `t_demos` exercises exactly this scenario:

| Node | Runtime | Flake | Expectation |
|------|---------|-------|-------------|
| a | Python | default (project) | pandas from UV — works before fix |
| b | T | default | basic T — unaffected |
| c | R | `github:jbedo/rshells` | R via custom flake — unaffected |
| d | Julia | `github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-24.11` | Julia via custom flake — unaffected |
| e | Python | `github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-24.11` | pandas from UV via custom flake — **fails before fix, works after** |

To verify:

```bash
cd py_uv_per_flake_t
nix develop --command t run src/pipeline.t
```

All 5 nodes should build successfully and all assertions should pass.
